54 /**
55 * @brief Layout that specifies how to map multi-dimensional indices to a linear/flat index.
56 *
57 * @details It stores the shape of the array, i.e. the length of each dimension, and the strides of each dimension.
58 * The stride of dimension `i` is the number of elements to skip in memory when the index of dimension `i` is
59 * incremented by one. For example:
60 * - To iterate over every element of a 5x5x5 array in C-order use the strides `(25, 5, 1)`.
61 * - To iterate over every 2nd element of a 1D array use the stride `(2)`.
62 * - To iterate over every 2nd column of a 10x10 array in Fortran-order use the strides `(1, 20)`.
63 * - To iterate over every 2nd row of a 10x10 array in Fortran-order use the strides `(2, 10)`.
64 *
65 * The template parameters `StaticExtents` and `StrideOrder` are encoded as `uint64_t`. They can be decoded to a
66 * `std::array<int, Rank>` using the nda::decode function. The encoding limits the number of dimensions, i.e. the
67 * rank, to 8.
68 *
69 * The static extent array specifies the length of each dimension at compile-time. A zero value means that the length
70 * in this dimension is dynamic and will be specified at runtime. Note that static lengths cannot exceed 255 (due to
71 * the encoding). For example:
72 * - `StaticExtents = nda::encode(std::array<int, Rank>{0, 10, 0, 5})` corresponds to a 4D array with dynamic extents
73 * in dimension 0 and 2, and static extents of length 10 and 5 in dimension 1 and 3, respectively.
74 *
75 * The stride order specifies the order in which the dimensions are stored in memory. In its array form, it can be any
76 * permutation of the integer values from `0` to `Rank - 1`. The slowest varying dimension is the first element of the
77 * array and the fastest varying dimension is the last element of the array. For example:
78 * - C-order: `StrideOrder = nda::encode(std::array<int, Rank>{0, 1, ..., Rank - 2, Rank - 1})`.
79 * - Fortran-order: `StrideOrder = nda::encode(std::array<int, Rank>{Rank - 1, Rank - 2, ..., 1, 0})`.
80 *
81 * `LayoutProp` is an enum flag that can be used to make further compile-time guarantees about the layout of the data
82 * in memory (see nda::layout_prop_e).
83 *
84 * @tparam Rank Number of dimensions.
85 * @tparam StaticExtent Compile-time known shape (zero if fully dynamic).
86 * @tparam StrideOrder Order in which the dimensions are stored in memory.
87 * @tparam LayoutProp Compile-time guarantees about the layout of the data in memory.
88 */
89 template <int Rank, uint64_t StaticExtents, uint64_t StrideOrder, layout_prop_e LayoutProp>
90 class idx_map {
91 static_assert(Rank <= 8, "Error in nda::idx_map: Rank must be <= 8");

93
94 // Extents of all dimensions (the shape of the map).

96
97 // Strides of all dimensions.

99
100 public:
101 /// Encoded static extents.
102 static constexpr uint64_t static_extents_encoded = StaticExtents;
103
104 /// Decoded static extents.

106
107 /// Decoded stride order.
108 static constexpr std::array<int, Rank> stride_order = (StrideOrder == 0 ? permutations::identity<Rank>() : decode<Rank>(StrideOrder));
109
110 /// Encoded stride order.
111 static constexpr uint64_t stride_order_encoded = encode(stride_order);
112
113 /// Compile-time memory layout properties.
114 static constexpr layout_prop_e layout_prop = LayoutProp;

116 /// Compile-time information about the layout (stride order and layout properties).

287 // Combine static and dynamic extents.
288 static std::array<long, Rank> merge_static_and_dynamic_extents(std::array<long, n_dynamic_extents> const &dynamic_extents) {
289 std::array<long, Rank> extents;
290 for (int u = 0, v = 0; u < Rank; ++u) extents[u] = (static_extents[u] == 0 ? dynamic_extents[v++] : static_extents[u]);
291 return extents;
292 }

450 [[nodiscard]] FORCEINLINE long myget(long arg) const noexcept {

452 // optimize for the case when the fastest varying dimension is contiguous in memory

464 template <typename... Args, size_t... Is>
465 [[nodiscard]] FORCEINLINE long call_impl(std::index_sequence<Is...>, Args... args) const noexcept {
466 // set e_pos to the position of the ellipsis, otherwise to -1
467 static constexpr int e_pos = ((std::is_same_v<Args, ellipsis> ? int(Is) + 1 : 0) + ...) - 1;
468
469 if constexpr (e_pos == -1) {
470 // no ellipsis present
471 if constexpr (smallest_stride_is_one) {
472 // optimize for the case that the fastest varying dimension is contiguous in memory

474 } else {
475 // arbitrary layouts

477 }
478 } else {
479 // empty ellipsis is present and needs to be skipped
480 15 return (myget<smallest_stride_is_one, (Is < e_pos ? Is : Is - 1)>(args) + ...);

582 * @brief Create a new map by permuting the indices/dimensions of the current map with a given permutation.
583 *
584 * @details Let \f$ A \f$ be the current and \f$ A' \f$ the new, permuted index map. \f$ P \f$ is the given
585 * permutation. We define the permuted nda::idx_map \f$ A' \f$ to be the one with the following properties:
586 * - \f$ A'(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1}) = A(i_{P[0]},\ldots,i_{P[n-1]}) \f$
587 * - \f$ A'.\text{lengths}()[k] = A.\text{lengths}()[P^{-1}[k]] \f$
588 * - \f$ A'.\text{strides}()[k] = A.\text{strides}()[P^{-1}[k]] \f$

590 * the stride order itself is a permutation).

601 // Note that this convention is the correct one to have a (left) action of the symmetric group on
602 // an array and it may not be completely obvious.
603 // Proof
604 // let's operate with P then Q, and denote A'' = Q A'. We want to show that A'' = (QP) A
605 // A'(i_k) = A(i_{P[k]})
606 // A''(j_k) = A'(j_{Q[k]})
607 // then i_k = j_{Q[k]} and A''(j_k) = A(i_{P[k]}) = A(j_{Q[P[k]]}) = A(j_{(QP)[k]}), q.e.d
608 //
609 // NB test will test this composition

613 //
614 // where S[k] denotes the strides.

617 // A'(i_k) = sum_k i_{P[k]} * S[k] = sum_k i_k * S[P^{-1}[k]]
618 // so
619 // S'[k] = S[P^{-1}[k]] (2)
620 // i.e. apply (inverse(P), S) or apply_inverse directly.
621 //
622 // 2- L' : lengths of A'
623 // if L[k] is the k-th length, then because of the definition of A', i.e. A'(i_k) = A(i_{P[k]})
624 // i_q in the lhs A is at position q' such that P[q'] = q (A'(i0 i1 i2...) = A( i_P0 i_P1 i_P2....)

629 // by definition Q is a permutation such that Q[0] is the slowest index, Q[Rank -1] the fastest
630 // hence S[Q[k]] is a strictly decreasing sequence (as checked by strides_compatible_to_stride_order)

634 // so the permutation Q' is such that P^{-1}Q' = Q or Q' = PQ (as permutation product/composition).
635 // NB : Q and P are permutations, so the operation must be a composition, not an apply (apply applies
